item.subject: science
item.stem:
Eshan sees wriggling mosquito larvae in stagnant water left in an unused clay pot in his courtyard in Thrissur. His teacher says a thin layer of kerosene on the water surface can stop them becoming adults.

Why does the kerosene layer work?

options.A: It makes the water look shiny, so adult mosquitoes refuse to lay more eggs there.
options.B: Larvae and pupae must reach air at the surface to breathe; the kerosene film blocks that air contact and disrupts development before adulthood.
options.C: Adult mosquitoes also need to dive under the kerosene to breathe, so the layer kills flying adults in the courtyard.
options.D: Kerosene is transparent, so air still reaches the larvae and the layer cannot affect breathing.
